recognize_zh: 多顆紅血球內含細小、藍色環狀的寄生蟲，有時一顆紅血球內有多個或呈成對梨形；右下插圖可見四個蟲體排成十字形（Maltese cross，四聯體），而且沒有瘧原蟲的色素或配子體，符合巴貝西蟲症（babesiosis）。
features: Small intraerythrocytic ring forms with delicate blue cytoplasm and tiny chromatin dots
Some red cells contain multiple parasites, including paired and pleomorphic forms
Tetrad arrangement (Maltese cross) visible in the inset
No hemozoin pigment, Schüffner dots or gametocytes; infected red cells are not enlarged
Background shows red cell anisocytosis with some microspherocytic/dense cells and occasional crenated cells; scattered platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cell anisocytosis with scattered dense cells and small intraerythrocytic parasites. The organisms are small ring forms and pleomorphic piriform forms, several red cells harbor more than one parasite, and the inset shows a characteristic tetrad (Maltese cross) arrangement. Infected cells are not enlarged, and no malarial pigment, stippling or gametocytes are identified. Findings are consistent with babesiosis; parasitemia should be quantified and confirmed by PCR, particularly given the post-transplant, transfusion-exposed setting.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum shows ring forms with applique and double chromatin dots, banana-shaped gametocytes and hemozoin pigment, but never tetrads.
Superimposed platelets have granular purple centers, lie in a different focal plane and often show a halo, lacking a blue ring cytoplasm with chromatin dot.
These inclusions are solid dark basophilic dots (single for Howell-Jolly, clustered peripheral for Pappenheimer) without a ring or vacuolated center.
